title: Mixtral of Experts
authors: Albert Q. Jiang, Alexandre Sablayrolles, Antoine Roux, Arthur Mensch, Blanche Savary, Chris Bamford, Devendra Singh Chaplot, Diego de las Casas, Emma Bou Hanna, Florian Bressand, Gianna Lengyel, Guillaume Bour, Guillaume Lample, Lélio Renard Lavaud, Lucile Saulnier, Marie-Anne Lachaux, Pierre Stock, Sandeep Subramanian, Sophia Yang, Szymon Antoniak, Teven Le Scao, Théophile Gervet, Thibaut Lavril, Thomas Wang, Timothée Lacroix, William El Sayed
date: January 2024 (arXiv v1 8 January 2024, the only version; weights released by magnet link on 8 December 2023, blog post 11 December 2023)
paper_note: 13 pages, 6 sections and two appendix figures

code.title: mistral-src
code.note: the reference inference code linked from the paper (repo, about 20 minutes for the README and entry path); it now redirects to mistral-inference, Apache 2.0, archived

takeaway: First open-weights SMoE (8 experts, top-2, 13B active/47B total) to match Llama 2 70B and GPT-3.5 at 5x fewer active params, with experts specialising on syntax and position rather than domain; kicked off the open-MoE era.
verdict: Believe the headline against Llama 2 70B: both were re-run on one pipeline and the wins on maths and code are large. Read "matches GPT-3.5" as a comparison with numbers copied from another report, "the speed of a 12.9B model" as true only at batch size 1 or very large batches, and the routing analysis as a small qualitative study with a baseline that assumes uniform expert use.

live.text: route text through a toy Mixtral

headline.d: recounted from Table 1 and the released config; 8 copies of the FFN only, attention shared

headline.k: against Llama 2 70B's 69.9% on the same pipeline
headline.d: with 5.4x fewer active parameters; +14.6 points on MATH, +10.9 on code
first open-weights model above GPT-3.5-Turbo (1117), trained with SFT then DPO

resources.n: the canonical MoE explainer, written for the Mixtral release; covers routing, load balancing, expert parallelism, and MoE fine-tuning gotchas (instability, router sensitivity) directly relevant to anyone tuning these models.

resources.t: A Visual Guide to Mixture of Experts
resources.n: the best diagrams of the router, top-K gating, and capacity concepts; ends with a Mixtral walkthrough.
traces the lineage from sparsely-gated MoE and Switch through Mixtral to modern fine-grained designs, with the math for sparse vs active parameter counts.

concise statement of the cost-performance claim and the serving story (vLLM + Megablocks, Skypilot deployment); the paper's webpage link, and the source of the "6x faster inference" and "same speed as a 12.9B model" claims this page tests.

release-day guide: what is unknown (pretraining data, fine-tuning data and hyperparameters), memory needed at each precision (over 90 GB in float16, over 23 GB in 4-bit), inference and fine-tuning code.

resources.t: Fast Inference of Mixture-of-Experts Language Models with Offloading
resources.n: the paper's reference [11]: runs Mixtral on consumer GPUs by caching recently used experts, the use of temporal locality that Section 5 points to; code at github.com/dvmazur/mixtral-offloading.

kb.n: 2021: the top-1 MoE predecessor, with a Switch layer you can train live; Mixtral's top-2, every-layer, no-fuss variant is what finally made the idea land in open weights.
2024: the next generation of open MoE; fine-grained experts, shared experts and auxiliary-loss-free balancing, a different answer to the coarse-expert regime documented here.
2023: Mixtral Instruct was among the first flagship models aligned with SFT plus DPO only.
2023: Mistral upstreamed Megablocks-based MoE kernels into vLLM to make the model servable at release.
2017: the Transformer whose feed-forward sub-block the MoE layer replaces.
2025: an open MoE family two years on (128 experts, 8 active), the fine-grained design that replaced eight big experts.

kb.t: Bounding the memory bottlenecks of large mixture-of-experts training
kb.n: the memory side of training MoE models: total parameters set the bill, which Mixtral's 47B against 13B makes concrete.

topics.n: the generic MoE layer: router, top-k styles, load balancing, capacity, expert parallelism, decode arithmetic.
the lab page: Mixtral's block animated against Mistral 7B and Small 4 at one scale, Table 5 charted, and where Mistral went next.
SFT and DPO, expert parallelism and distributed training.
serving MoE models: batching, expert parallelism, offloading.
